answer.decision: Choose jittered expirations, request coalescing, and stale-while-revalidate.
answer.action: Today, enable the cache client's single-flight primitive for this endpoint and serve stale values for up to 90 seconds while one request refreshes each key. Then add randomized TTL jitter so hot keys do not expire together, set TTL and refresh timing to guarantee data is never more than five minutes old, add metrics for coalesced requests, stale serves, cache hit rate, origin requests by key, and refresh failures, and load-test the 120 hottest keys before full rollout.
reasons: Duplicate queries for the same 120 keys caused 91 percent of the origin CPU spike, so coalescing directly addresses the dominant load source.
The existing disabled single-flight primitive enables an immediate mitigation without replacing the cache product.
Jitter prevents synchronized deterministic expirations, while stale-while-revalidate avoids sending concurrent misses to the origin during refresh.
Up to 90 seconds of stale serving is explicitly acceptable and can be configured within the five-minute freshness requirement.
Database scaling alone improved latency but still saturated under duplicate traffic; globally increasing TTL risks violating the freshness bound.
assumptions: The single-flight primitive can be enabled or narrowly integrated today for the affected endpoint.
TTL jitter and stale-while-revalidate can be configured per entry or implemented around the existing cache client.
The five-minute bound measures the age of the served data, including any stale-while-revalidate window.
risks: Single-flight failures or timeouts could block many callers unless bounded with timeouts and fallback behavior.
Poorly selected TTL and stale windows could exceed the five-minute freshness bound.
Jitter alone does not protect against simultaneous cold starts or evictions, so request coalescing must remain enabled.
Serving stale data during repeated refresh failures could require rejecting requests once the five-minute limit is reached.

citations.claim: Repeated queries for the same 120 keys accounted for 91 percent of the origin CPU spike.
The cache client already provides a disabled single-flight primitive.
The endpoint must preserve freshness within five minutes.
Database scaling improved latency but did not prevent saturation from duplicate requests.
Stale values may be served for up to 90 seconds during refresh if the five-minute bound is maintained.
